thread.title: Tech Today: Intel New Highs, Western Downgraded, Amazon’s Trade $$, Twitter’s Reprieve

author: Tiernan Ray
title: Tech Today: Intel New Highs, Western Downgraded, Amazon’s Trade $$, Twitter’s Reprieve
text:
Intel's chief executive Brian Krzanich discusses the data cloud during his keynote at CES 2018 in Las Vegas. Photo by Tiernan Ray for Barron's. Here are some things going on today in your world of tech :
Shares of Intel ( INTC ) are $4.53, or 10%, at $49.82, headed towards its highest closing price since 2000 , after the company yesterday afternoon beat Q4 revenue and earnings expectations comfortably, boosted by its non-PC, "data-centric” businesses, raised its dividend by 10%, and offered an outlook for the quarter and the year that was also better than expected.
Price targets are on the rise at several shops, and the stock has gotten at least one upgrade, that I can see, from Credit Suisse ’s John Pitzer , who raises his rating to Outperform from Neutral. Pitzer deems his own $55 price target, representing 19 times as a multiple of enterprise value times free cash flow as “high,” but given "better execution, conservative estimates, and significant investor skepticism, we are willing to suffer thru high valuation,” he writes.
For the bears, Mark Lipacis of Jefferies & Co. reiterates his Sell rating, noting the outlook for Q1’s earnings of 65 cents to 75 cents is actually two cents below consensus. He thinks that gross profit margins will fall two percentage points this year, as “capital intensity” increases, and that Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ), and CPU cores from ARM , will “start taking material share by the second half of 2018."
Shares of Western Digital ( WDC ) are up 17 cents, or $88.16, recovering from yesterday evening’s sell-off following its fiscal Q2 results, as its conference call with investors and Q3 outlook seemed to ease some concerns about hard drives and flash. But price targets are coming down, and the stock has gotten one downgrade this morning, from Summit Redstone ’s Kinngai Chan , who cut the stock to Hold from Buy, “as we see a high risk of gross margin compression given that the recent industry pricing dynamics in the NAND flash/client SSD market."
Amidst continued chatter about Apple ( AAPL ) iPhone sales potentially falling short of expectations, Rosenblatt Securities ’s Jun Zhang rejects such talk and reiterates his Buy rating, and $180 price target, writing that although the forecast for the March quarter, when Apple reports on February 1st, may be below Street expectations, “we are not as bearish as some since it’s our view that the company should recognize a portion of the iPhone X units that were produced in December and iPhone SE2 shipments” and that there may yet be “upside” from the impending retail availability of the “ HomePod ” speaker.
Apple shares are up a penny at $171.12.
Shares of Amazon ( AMZN ) are up $21.82, or 1.6%, at $1,399.68, after Morgan Stanley ’s Brian Nowak reiterated an Overweight rating on the stock, and raised his price target to $1,400 from $1,250, and raised his “bull case” to $2,100, writing that the company’s opportunity in advertising is turning out to be larger than he thought.
He raises his estimates after concluding that Amazon has a particularly good opportunity to capture what are called “trade spend,” the dollars that consumer packaged goods brands pay to retailers “to promote inventory through their channels in the form of promotional allowances (i.e. coupons for consumers) and vendor allowances (e.g., slotting fees on shelves/end caps, and volume purchase thresholds)."
Former Twitter ( TWTR ) CEO Dick Costolo was on CNBC with host Carl Quintanilla this morning, downplaying the matter of Twitter COO Anthony Noto leaving the company. He said more important for Twitter is Facebook ’s ( FB ) recent decision to change the “ newsfeed ” feature on its property to be less about news, more about personal, friends and family kind of content, as Costolo sees it. “This is huge” for Twitter, and very positive, because Facebook’s pushing of news was like Facebook “digging in Twitter’s backyard,” so he expects it will help Twitter.
In other Twitter chatter, Briefing.com was relaying this morning renewed takeover rumors, again mentioning Salesforce ( CRM ) as a potential bidder. In a brief item this afternoon, CFRA Research 's Scott Kessler reiterates a Strong Sell rating on Twitter, writing "we do not think Salesforce is going to buy Twitter." He points out the reaction in 2016 on such speculation was negative for Salesforce's stock, there are "limited synergies," and takes Noto's departure as a sign of "significant" uncertainties at Twitter.
Twitter stock is up $1.36, or 6%, at $23.52.
